title: Support criterion for restriction of a right adjoint to a quasi-compact open
statement: Let f:X\to Y be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let a be the right adjoint to Rf_* on quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image], and let V\subset Y be a quasi-compact open with inverse image U=f^{-1}(V)\subset X, with open immersions j:V\to Y and j_U:U\to X. Let a_V be the right adjoint for the restriction f|_U:U\to V. The canonical open-square map j_U^*a(K)\to a_V(Lj^*K) is an isomorphism for every K\in D_QCoh^+(Y) if and only if a(Q) is supported on X\setminus U for every Q\in D_QCoh^+(Y) supported on Y\setminus V. The same equivalence holds with D_QCoh(Y) in place of D_QCoh^+(Y). If a commutes with all set-indexed direct sums, the bounded-below equivalent conditions imply (and hence are equivalent to) the unbounded equivalent conditions.

proof.text: The open square gives the canonical transformation j_U^*a(K) \to a_V(Lj^*K) by transposing the open-square base-change map and composing with the unit K \to Rj_*Lj^*K and the counit j_U^*Rj_{U,*} \to id. Restriction to an open preserves K-injective complexes [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open], so computing Rf_* with a K-injective resolution gives (Rf_*N)|_V\cong R(f|_U)_*(N|_U) for N in D_QCoh(X). Hence for L in D_QCoh(V) and N in D_QCoh(X), Hom(N,a(Rj_*L))=Hom((Rf_*N)|_V,L)=Hom(R(f|_U)_*(N|_U),L)=Hom(N,Rj_{U,*}a_V(L)), so a(Rj_*L)\cong Rj_{U,*}a_V(L) and, as j_U^*Rj_{U,*}\cong id, a(Rj_*L)|_U\cong a_V(L). With L=Lj^*K this transformation is therefore an isomorphism exactly when the map a(K)|_U \to a(Rj_*Lj^*K)|_U induced by the unit is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For K in D_QCoh^+(Y), use the distinguished triangle K \to Rj_*Lj^*K \to Q \to K[1] from [lem-sc-open-restriction-support-triangle]; its third term is again bounded below and supported on Y\setminus V. Applying the triangulated functor a gives a(K) \to a(Rj_*Lj^*K) \to a(Q) \to a(K)[1]. If a(Q) is supported on X\setminus U for every such Q, restriction to U kills the third term, so the map in Step 1 is an isomorphism for every K. Conversely, for Q supported on Y\setminus V, apply the assumed isomorphism to K=Q; since Lj^*Q=0, the triangle identifies the restriction of a(Q) to U with zero, so a(Q) is supported on X\setminus U. This proves (i). The same argument for arbitrary K\in D_QCoh(Y), using the all-complexes clause of [lem-sc-open-restriction-support-triangle], proves the equivalence in (ii).

Assume a commutes with all set-indexed direct sums and that the bounded-below equivalent conditions hold. Let T=Y\setminus V and let D be the full saturated triangulated subcategory of the complexes in D_QCoh(Y) whose cohomology is supported on T and for which a(Q) is supported on X\setminus U. Preservation of direct sums by a makes D closed under direct sums and the derived colimits used below. By [lem-sc-supported-derived-generated-perfect], the supported subcategory is generated by a perfect object E, and every supported object is a derived colimit of a sequence whose successive cones are direct sums of shifts of E. Since E is bounded below and supported on T, the bounded-below condition gives E\in D; closure under shifts, cones, retracts, and direct sums gives every stage in D, and closure under the final derived colimit gives every supported Q\in D. Thus the unbounded support condition follows, and Step 2 gives the unbounded restriction isomorphism. The converse implications follow by restricting the unbounded assertions to D_QCoh^+(Y).
